experiment: RoPE frequency sweep on skip3 (content-neutral: query token independent of target s[i-k])
purpose: search for a discriminating cell where alpha_L beats the relative/absolute taxonomy (B2a)
verdict: NEGATIVE. No discriminating cell. At scale 0.03 alpha_L=0 but LG=0.88 -> alpha_L FALSE NEGATIVE: the trained softmax head resolves the offset via a kernel the linear-kernel fit deems unrealizable. At scale 0.01 the model cannot learn even in-distribution (train 0.23) so it is excluded by the learnability filter. Conclusion: alpha_L UNDER-predicts low-frequency relative PEs; the relative/absolute taxonomy ('relative -> generalizes bounded offsets') is correct across the resolvable range; the predictor does not beat the taxonomy. This corrects the earlier 'content rescue' label for low-freq RoPE: skip-k is content-neutral, so this is positional under-prediction, not content.
